function: Over-the-air FL aggregation: aggregate beamforming plus device selection, minimizing aggregate MSE or maximizing selected devices under an MSE limit (p. 5, 9-10).
system: K single-antenna devices, aggregator with N antennas (N much smaller than K, N=2 to 12 simulated); no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 6, 25).
method: Non-learned random aggregate beamforming (uniform sample on complex unit sphere, then top-S devices), refined with Nm draws; FL training of MLP and ResNet18 (p. 11, 17, 27).
data_channel: Synthetic i.i.d. Rayleigh channels h_k ~ CN(0, I), Monte Carlo (p. 7, 22); FL on non-i.i.d. MNIST (MLP) and CIFAR10 (ResNet18), aggregate error modeled as retransmission (p. 27).
test_conditions: No channel training; same Rayleigh model throughout, sweeping N, K, S, MSE threshold and Nm (pp. 22-26); FL test accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR10 (p. 27).
baselines: Non-learned: random device selection with DC beamforming, iterative selection with DC beamforming (pp. 21-22), l1+SDR [34]; earlier published design: DC algorithm [24] (p. 22). No learned PHY baseline.
metrics: Aggregate MSE/sigma^2, number of selected devices, empirical versus theoretical CDF and PMF, FL test accuracy (pp. 22-28).
complexity: Order of complexity: O(K) for the proposed scheme and O(Nm K) for the refined one, negligible against DC and l1+SDR; no runtime reported (p. 11, 21, 26).
q1_support: p. 7: "Gaussian distributed with unit power". Channels are i.i.d. complex Gaussian (Rayleigh) from a custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 24: "we conduct simulations for 100 channel realizations". Nothing is trained on channels: sweeps over N, K, S and the MSE threshold test a non-learned design, and the FL model is evaluated on MNIST and CIFAR10 only; no unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 22: "A novel DC algorithm [24]" is an earlier published aggregation design; non-learned: "Random device selection and aggregate beamforming design" and l1+SDR [34]. The paper's own Benchmark1 and Benchmark2 heuristics are not counted.
q4_support: p. 21: "have a computational complexity of O (K), and thereby the required computational complexity for the refined methods is O (Nm K)". Order of complexity of the beamforming and selection design; no runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 27: "datasets, i.e., MNIST10 and CIFAR10". These are learning-task datasets only; the channels are simulated (p. 7) and no code or data link is given.
notes: Include, area 7: joint device selection and aggregate beamforming for AirComp FL (p. 5, 9); the aggregator has N antennas (p. 6), so the system check passes. Caveat for the reviewer: the beamformer is random sampling, not learned, so no_learning passes only through the FL-over-the-air rule. The effect of the aggregate error on FL is simulated as retransmission with probability 1-exp(-a MSE/sigma^2) (p. 27). q3 rests on [24] as the earlier published aggregation design, which is optimization-based. PDF is arXiv 2403.18946v1, same title, formatted as IEEE TWC.
